item.title: Water pollution in DRC attributed to Chinese mining company
item.description: While areas rich in rare minerals may be a blessing for the country’s economy, they can also be a curse for the local populations in the DRC.

item.title: Nigerian Muslim and Christian peace advocates call for calm, unity amid US designation as a ‘Country of Particular Concern’
item.description: “For decades, Nigerians have lived side by side in peace. Our unity is our strength, allowing foreign interests to divide us would be the greatest tragedy of all.”

item.title: When dreams meet digital recruitment scams: Bangladeshi workers in crisis
item.description: Bangladeshi migrant workers face rising digital scams exploiting limited digital literacy, informal brokers, and weak coordination among government agencies, leaving thousands stranded and in debt annually.

item.title: Samoa prime minister bans newspaper from attending press briefings
item.description: “Banning an entire news organization from press conferences hurts the public interest as people will lose access to independent reporting on matters of national importance.”

item.title: Critics say Hong Kong fire was due to negligence, not scaffolding
item.description: What we need includes an independent investigation into the malpractice surrounding repair project bidding, the failure of the current monitoring system and the inaction of government authorities upon receiving complaints.

item.title: Pakistani travellers with valid visas being quietly offloaded at airports in ‘silent ban’
item.description: Pakistan has tightened airport screenings to help combat trafficking, but the new measures increasingly trouble lawful travellers, eroding rights, and livelihoods as communities experience profiling, and measures that deepen resentment.

item.title: Stuck between survival and modesty: How an earthquake revealed Bangladesh’s gender fault line
item.description: As tremors rippled across Bangladesh, panic sent people fleeing into the streets, yet online debates fixated not on safety but on whether women should cover themselves before escaping collapsing buildings.

item.title: The sentence demanded in the case of jailed Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu is 2,430 years
item.description: The opposition Republican People's Party (CHP), which İmamoğlu represents, has condemned the case as politically driven — arguing the timing and scope are aimed at sidelining a major political opponent.

item.title: Participatory monitoring breathes life into Cameroon’s Marine Protected Areas
item.description: The marine protected area faces several challenges — ones that the local communities are working hard to mitigate through participatory monitoring. Yet the protected area continues to face threats.

item.title: Queer cinema in Azerbaijan tells stories of visibility and survival
item.description: These films transform personal struggles into collective narratives, illustrating how survival, memory, and the quest for belonging are intertwined with the creation of queer cinematic histories.
